sketches.mechanism: The Maybe monad's fromMaybe function, which provides a default when something is absent — combined with the fact that Nothing is a literal constructor in Haskell
sketches.resonance: When you lose someone, you replace their absence with whatever you can bear, but the type system remembers it was always a Maybe.
sketches.draft:
you :: Maybe a
you = Nothing

me :: a -> a
me = fromMaybe (me undefined)

sketches.mechanism: Weak references automatically become nil when the object they point to is deallocated — the runtime erases what you held without warning
sketches.resonance: A weak reference is a bond that cannot prevent loss; the system reclaims what it will, and you are left holding nil.

sketches.mechanism: A function declared with a return type but containing no return statement — undefined behavior in C, where the caller receives whatever happened to be in the register
sketches.resonance: A promise was made by the signature, but nothing was actually given back; the caller trusts the shape of something that was never filled.
